fix.shows: The Hindu read Delhi's draft roll of 97.54 lakh electors, matched it to the lists of the 33.12 lakh sent notices (13.79 lakh unmapped with the last SIR and 19.33 lakh for logical discrepancies), and guessed each elector's religion from their name and their relative's name. On that guess, Muslims were 13.6% of the draft roll, 7.6% of the unmapped and 20.3% of those flagged for logical discrepancies, and 30% of those flagged for the five reasons that turn on family size, such as six or more electors naming the same parent. The paper reports that ERONET, the Commission's software, decided who was flagged, that no SIR order mentioned notices for discrepancies before the Commission's direction of 14 May 2026, which still did not set out the reasons, and that the Commission had not answered its questions.
